item.title: [ZEPPELIN-358] Jetty server is HTTP ERROR 404
item.description:
Sometimes Zeppelin Jetty Server is HTTP Error 404.
But, Zeppelin interpreter still work. (Zeppelin cron job still work.)
I can not access Zeppelin GUI.

HTTP ERROR 404

Problem accessing /. Reason:

    Not Found
Powered by Jetty://

Why do happened?

status.description: A resolution has been taken, and it is awaiting verification by reporter. From here issues are either reopened, or are closed.

Your attached log has no problem.

One possible theory is,
If you're using Zeppelin-0.5.0-incubating-bin release, it packages webapp to war and Jetty caches it's resource under /tmp/jetty-* directory when running it.
Then your /etc/cron.daily/tmpwatch kicks in and remove the jetty cache dir. Then it would cause 404 not found for webapp resources.

Thnaks for your reply.
If I have a same problem, I will try.

When I remove /tmp/jetty-* directory, Zeppelin jetty server is down.

HTTP ERROR 404

Problem accessing /. Reason:

    Not Found
Powered by Jetty://

So, I check my /etc/cron.daily/tmpwatch file.
But, I do not know what is problem.
Can you help me?

#! /bin/sh                                                             
flags=-umc                                                             
/usr/sbin/tmpwatch "$flags" -x /tmp/.X11-unix -x /tmp/.XIM-unix \      
        -x /tmp/.font-unix -x /tmp/.ICE-unix -x /tmp/.Test-unix \      
        -X '/tmp/hsperfdata_*' 10d /tmp                                
/usr/sbin/tmpwatch "$flags" 30d /var/tmp                               
for d in /var/{cache/man,catman}/{cat?,X11R6/cat?,local/cat?}; do      
    if [ -d "$d" ]; then                                               
        /usr/sbin/tmpwatch "$flags" -f 30d "$d"                        
    fi                                                                 
done

Where is the problem line? and Do you have a plan fix this problem?
Or Already fix this problem at next version?

Hello,
I just solved the same problem.

In my case, I just changed zeppelin.server.port in zeppelin-site.xml from 8080 to 8000. Something was maybe kind of blocking it (may be some older instance of zeppelin, but not sure though). I believe a server restart might help, but zeppelin is not the only service in my case and I didn't want to irritate admin.

Hello, Thanks for an advice.
In my case, Zeppelin port is 9090. (8000 port is already use in my server.) But also Zeppelin jetty directory has gone.
So I have to find another solutions.
I wonder if it is only solution that Zeppelin restart.

Hadoop Project also use jetty.
but I couldn't have experience that webapp folder of hadoop vanish.
That's why hadoop jetty is not vanishing.
Hadoop use embedded jetty.
If Zeppelin use embedded jetty and doesn't create /tmp/jetty-* folder, Zeppelin Server wouldn't be down.
So I want to try applying Zeppelin use embedded jetty and does not create ' /tmp/jetty-*' folder.
Is it okay?
If you can make Zeppelin embedded avoid creating directory under '/tmp/jetty-*', that would be helpful.

When I download Zeppelin-bin. It has 'zeppelin-web-version-incubating.war' file.
So jetty need to temporary directories because war file included.
If zeppelin contain source file instead of war, jetty does not create temporary directories.
Or zeppelin define local temp file path (if do not want to create temporary directories).
I have two choices.
One is define jetty local temp directories path. other is that do not contain war file.
What is prefer?
http://www.eclipse.org/jetty/documentation/current/ref-temporary-directories.html

I would like to define jetty local temp directories.
Is it fine?
But I am not sure it is fix vanishing webapps directories.
Add unnecessary comments.. Absolutely vanishing Zeppelin webapps directories are bothering.

GitHub user mwkang opened a pull request:

https://github.com/apache/incubator-zeppelin/pull/498

ZEPPELIN-358: Jetty server is HTTP ERROR 404

Define local jetty temp directory.
`varName: zeppelin.war.tempdir`
`default varValue: webapps`
Zeppelin create temp directory in `

{zeppelin.home}

/webapps` when zeppelin server start.
